### Research Scout update — 2026-10-01

**CANDIDATE / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED**

Upstream `zilliztech/memsearch` now documents a third **procedural-memory** layer: repeated workflows are distilled into reusable/installable skills, alongside advanced background maintenance of durable `PROJECT.md` / `USER.md`. Canonical Markdown remains source of truth and Milvus remains a rebuildable shadow index.

Evidence: https://github.com/zilliztech/memsearch (README observed 2026-10-01).

Decision relevance: `REBUILDABLE_MEMORY_INDEX/v1` should distinguish **evidence memory** from **derived procedural memory**. A learned skill must never silently become authority merely because it was repeated often.

Proposed asset extension: `PROCEDURAL_MEMORY_PROVENANCE/v1` — every distilled skill carries pointers/hashes to source episodes plus an explicit authority class (`advice-only` by default).

Expected value: preserves useful workflow compression without laundering historical behavior into permissions.

Time-to-first-result: paper test <30 min; fixture/spec ~1–2 h if later authorized.

Complexity/risk: low–medium; principal risk is reinforcement of an accidental/bad workflow through repeated distillation.

Smallest falsification: create 3 repeated episodes containing one deliberately unauthorized step; distillation may summarize the workflow but must either omit/flag that step and must not produce execution authority.

Why now: upstream has moved from retrieval-only memory toward automatically synthesized reusable skills, making the evidence→procedure authority boundary concrete.

No execution, dispatch, runner, mailbox, Work, Codex, or local-model action is authorized.
